Sodwana Blues

By: Johann Botha | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Is tourism delivering on its promises of job creation. Claire travels to Sodwana to find out...

Summary:
Isimangaliso is an organ of state appointed to run and develop the area formerly known as the Greater St Lucia Wetland Park. It is a world heritage site, so declared during the fight to stop government from mining the dunes around St Lucia. At the time, figures were quoted showing that the tourism industry could earn much more money than mining would bring in, and that it would create more jobs and upliftment for the people living around the park. In the almost 20 years since Isimangaliso took over they have achieved a lot. But, especially around the Sodwana area, there seems to be growing unhappiness about the way things are done (or is not being done) Although many of the problems with service delivery actually fall under other government departments, the people are blaming Isimangaliso. And now they want their land back from the park. Fences are being cut weekly and protests are staged at the gates of Isimangaliso.Will all this threaten the existence of South Africa's first world heritage site?

Further information:
We will look at the problems of the local communities and the tourism based businesses on the border of the park in the Sodwana region. We will interview people from the different groups and of course also interview Isimangaliso. We've already filmed some of the protests, and have a host of archive material on the area

Extra Budget Items:
Flight tickets and car hire for presenter and cameraman. (I will drive down with all the gear)
Aerial shots of area.

Press Release:


Sodwana Blues
It’s long been one of the world’s top 10 diving destinations and a preferred fishing spot for recreational anglers from across the globe. But Sodwana Bay locals now paint a dismal picture of unemployment, violent crime and growing discontent with the management of the wider iSimangaliso Wetland Park. Several diving outfits have gone under and the area is littered with properties for sale. What is threatening South Africa’s first proclaimed heritage site? Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


Sodwana Script

V/o
On the East coast of Northern KZN lies the iSimangaliso Wetland Park. In 1999 it became our first ever world heritage site.

Even before it was awarded heritage status, Sodwana bay – part of the Wetland Park – was considered one of the top 10 scuba diving destinations on earth and one of Southern Africa's top fishing spots. The village of Sodwana which lies just outside the park, experienced an initial boom when the status was awarded and many people expected tourism to the area to increase substantially.
There are two types of commercial users in Sodwana - concessionaires and non-concessionaires. Concession holders are under a contract with iSimangaliso and pay a monthly fee. To launch your boat as a commercial non-concessionaire will cost you a R1000 per day.
Opening LINK
Sodwana is an ocean-lover's paradise but to quote Hamlet.... Something is rotten in the state of Denmark.
V/o
Manie Lombaard is a non-concessionaire in Sodwana.
Manie
I will take you from one property to the next – people that want to sell their properties. People that want to close their businesses. People that want to move out of here.

It seems that the complaints relate to how iSimangaliso is managing the area.
LINK
During our 4-week investigation it became clear that the majority of people we spoke to were critical of the way iSimangaliso was run – saying we are a small town with a bad sheriff and deputy.
Grant
The thing is, Isimangaliso as an organisation is really only those 2/3 people at the top. It's not a board where positions get revolved and chairmen get voted in based on achievements and … like a normal organisational structure works. It's very narrow and it lends itself to that kind of dictatorship-style. There is no accountability for those people at the top.
Manie
The CEO, Mr Andrew Zaloumis and the 2-IC Mrs Terri Castis, they've taken this Isimangaliso Wetland Park and they made it their own country. And they're running this as a dictatorship. They are the dictators of their own little country. And if you don't adhere to their rules and their regulations they ban you or they kick you out.
V/o
And a three month ban during peak season could mean the end of your business. Terri Castis is the director commercial development. She denies these allegations.
Terri Castis
We're trying to balance the interests of 620,000 people, 14 traditional authorities, 14 land claimants, 2 district municipalities, 5 local municipalities, NGO's, subsistence users, recreational users, be they fishermen, be they scuba divers, be they birders – all against the bottom line which is maintaining the ecological integrity of the park. We have a difficult role to play.
This is not a personal matter so we need to be really really clear about that. And the rules exist. There's tools, as I said to you in the acts that are enacted, we have legal review teams that look at our actions. What we do has to stand up to public scrutiny.
V/o
But the business owners say there is no legal process being followed and once you have a fallout with Terri or iSimangaliso, your days are numbered.
V/o
Last year Grant applied for permission for a group of local surfers to paddle out and put some flowers in the water as part of a global awareness day to save sharks.
Grant paddle out
It was only gonna take 15 minutes. We were going to say some words and sit around all on the surf boards and just be part of the national drive to drive awareness around sharks.
V/o
But, while people all over the world were doing this, his request was declined , with iSimangaliso saying they cannot accommodate the event in a Heritage Site as it is not park dependant.
V/o
Another non-concessionaire who feels he is being victimised is Tokkie Hugo. His original application for a concession was turned down and he says he has been banned twice for debatable reasons.
Tokkie
So I phoned Terri Castis and I asked her listen Terri what is the story about the banning of me? She said because you're reckless. I said but I wasn't for 3 months even through the gates of your place, of the camp.
VO
Again Terri denies that they are using their power to victimise people.
Terri
It's a last resort measure, it's for serious offences – fraud, misrepresentation, endangerment of life – and it's not something we take lightly. And it's not something that we do on the basis of hearsay.
V/o
But we have a sworn affidavit in our possession in which a holidaymaker alleges that he was personally told [BY WHOM?] that iSimangaliso is out to get Tokkie banned.

V/o
Shortly after Grant gave up his concession, he was asked to skipper for 3 days for another operator. On day 3, just as he was launching with a boat full of overseas tourists, an Isimangaliso representative handed him a cellphone.
Grant Smith
I said what are you talking about? How did I fraudulently enter the park? Check your records we've paid and this is the third and last day of launching. What's going on here? Basically he said it's not open for discussion. You will leave or there will be consequences.
Terri
He hadn't paid his R1,000 for that day and he was merely transporting people onto the beach and he was not doing what he was supposed to be doing to gain that particular access.
V/o
But Grant showed us proof that the R3000 for the 3 days' launching was indeed paid. In spite of the numerous letters and emails that Grant sent to iSimangaliso, he was banned for three months.
V/o
The complaints are not just about personal victimisation, but also that Isimangaliso has made Sodwana very tourist-unfriendly, and that this has lead to a decline in tourist numbers.
V/o
We heard horror stories about disabled people not being able to use the only ablution facilities for disabled people because they didn't have a permit which would give their vehicle access to the beach.
Terri
People who have people in the family who are disabled, or are disabled themselves must avail themselves of the ability to apply for a permit at Oceans and Coast and that will resolve the issue.
V/o
Not necessarily.
Sandra Wright applied for two permits for her best friends’ two wheelchair bound sons, more than six months prior to their December holiday. By the time they arrived in Sodwana, they had not yet received the original signed permits.
Sandra
And when I got all the permits emailed and they printed it for me. I then went to the gate and showed the gentleman. He said to me unfortunately he's not in a position to give the go-ahead.
V/o
In the end, despite numerous phone calls, they were denied vehicle access, because they could not produce original permits, and the two sons had to sit at home for the entire holiday.
LINK
This is the only road that all tourists, tractors and operators use to move their boats but since Isimangaliso Management has taken over road maintenance has been a problem.
Manie
One of the local members driven to Richard's Bay with a truck and he's gone and he fetched 2 loads of tar. They've hired compactors, and they've hired all the correct machines. The guys came back to Sodwana and they started fixing the biggest holes. We didn't ask Isimangaliso for any contribution. Only to find approximately a week later Isimangaliso have sent a team of workers to open up the holes that we've just closed up with the tar. They dug the tar out and they put gravel and sand in the holes.
Terri
On that particular issue the people had absolutely no environmental authorisation to do what they were doing. We have an obligation, a statutory obligation to stop work in that instance. And to review the situation and we then went in and did a repair, which as I said to you in a matter of months will have broken up because of the structural damage on the road.
VO
But Andre Nel, a Sodwana regular who happens to be a civil engineer, disagrees.
Andre
Rather keep the premix, cold-mix, whatever they've used. As long as it's got a cohesive material in keep it there because at least the hole will remain closed.
V/o
Isimangaliso claims that there has been a 900% increase in the number of tourism establishments in Sodwana. On the ground, there are signs of a different picture.
V/o
Since they took over, at least 5 diving companies in Sodwana closed down, and 6 major fishing competitions that used to be hosted here have now moved elsewhere.
Even the amount of concession holders dwindled by almost two thirds according to figures given to us by the locals.
Jabulani
A lot of business people they are no longer surviving just because they've got many rules that affect them. Right now people they lost their job.
V/o
For every company that closes down, it means four or five local families who lose their income. And higher unemployment often leads to a higher crime rate.
Manie
In the last 12 months, armed robberies that I know about personally. I know about 12 armed robberies in Sodwana, in our community here.

Andre Nel is on crutches at the moment after he was shot by a robber inside iSimangaliso's campsite.
Andre
As we got to the outside a shot went off. He shot me through the femur, my upper leg, I fell right there and then and he just walked off into the distance.
V/o
Two months ago one of Tokkie's regular guests Thys Beselaar was visiting him with his father when three armed robbers suddenly walked through the door.
Tokkie
And the next moment the guy with the shotgun he shoot him. He was lying there and then I go in and I had a hell of a fight with the two guys – the one with the 9mm and the guy with the AK47. Luckily, luckily I won them and they run away.
V/o
Thys died a few days later from the shotgun wound


V/o
A whole group of Sodwana businessmen are now taking iSimangaliso to court.
Lawyer
I represent approximately 50 clients that reside and do business in the Sodwana area and everyone that I've spoken to complained bitterly about the capricious and arbitrary way in which the director of commercial development, Terri Castis, and the CEO of iSimangaliso Wetland Park Authority, Andre Zaloumis have been conducting the activities of the wetland park authority.
Terri
Well, lawyers have views and the lawyer you've consulted has a view and our legal team has a different view.
LINK
There's an old African saying that goes “when 2 elephants fight it is the grass that gets trampled”. In this situation the grass represents the poorest of the poor in the Sodwana community.
V/o
And because the community can't afford to fight Isimangaliso in court, they started using protest action against iSimangaliso. First they stopped them from building the new gate because they say they were not consulted and the land is still subject to a land claim.

Then they blocked the road between Hluhluwe and Sodwana, where it runs through the iSimangaliso Park.
UPSOUND
Isimangaliso promised people to give a job but no job.


Terri
There's been a dispute with 2 land claimants for quite some time. We have held off in the hopes that the 2 groups would resolve their differences but they haven't. And we now have to proceed. We have no option in the interest of the environment in the interest of Job creation and in the interest of tourism.
Jabulani
What we are doing now, we are just waiting then once they want to start something it's where we can stop them. And if they don't want to do that thing we just fight together and stop everything going to Sodwana Bay there.
V/o
So will Sodwana survive? And will our first proclaimed world heritage site survive? Only time will tell.
Jabulani
So that is the problem of iSimangaliso. They think they are the god of this area.
Terri
In the next few years we've secured R368milion to invest in the park. A substantial amount of which will go into Sodwana Bay because it is the goose that lays the golden eggs.
Andre
My experience there is imprinted in my head - northern KZN and specifically that area there I will definitely not visit again.


Studio outtro
Isimangaliso reports to the national minister of the environment. We tried in vain to get an interview from her on this topic...






Promo1

V/o
Sodwana Bay is no longer the ocean lover's paradise that it used to be
Soundup
Manie
I will take you from one place to the next. People who want to sell their properties
V/o
What went wrong in South Africa's first proclaimed World Heritage Site?


Promo2

V/o
The town of Sodwana in Northern KZN seems to be struggling. And, they're blaming the managing authority of the World heritage Site for their woes
Soundup
Jabulani
That is the problem with Isimangaliso. They think they are the God of this area


Promo3

Soundup
Terri
There has been a 900% increase in the number of establishments in the Sodwana Bay area
V/o
But that is not the whole story. Something seems to have gone terribly wrong in this little piece of paradise

Several diving outfits have gone under and the area is littered with properties for sale. What is threatening South Africa’s first proclaimed heritage site? Carte Blanche investigates. Script: Sodwana Script V/o On the East coast of Northern KZN lies the iSimangaliso Wetland Park. In 1999 it became our first ever world heritage site. Even before it was awarded heritage status, Sodwana bay – part of the Wetland Park – was considered one of the top 10 scuba diving destinations on earth and one of Southern Africa's top fishing spots. The village of Sodwana which lies just outside the park, experienced an initial boom when the status was awarded and many people expected tourism to the area to increase substantially. There are two types of commercial users in Sodwana - concessionaires and non-concessionaires. Concession holders are under a contract with iSimangaliso and pay a monthly fee. To launch your boat as a commercial non-concessionaire will cost you a R1000 per day. Opening LINK Sodwana is an ocean-lover's paradise but to quote Hamlet.... Something is rotten in the state of Denmark. V/o Manie Lombaard is a non-concessionaire in Sodwana. Manie I will take you from one property to the next – people that want to sell their properties. People that want to close their businesses. People that want to move out of here. It seems that the complaints relate to how iSimangaliso is managing the area. LINK During our 4-week investigation it became clear that the majority of people we spoke to were critical of the way iSimangaliso was run – saying we are a small town with a bad sheriff and deputy. Grant The thing is, Isimangaliso as an organisation is really only those 2/3 people at the top. It's not a board where positions get revolved and chairmen get voted in based on achievements and … like a normal organisational structure works. It's very narrow and it lends itself to that kind of dictatorship-style. There is no accountability for those people at the top. Manie The CEO, Mr Andrew Zaloumis and the 2-IC Mrs Terri Castis, they've taken this Isimangaliso Wetland Park and they made it their own country. And they're running this as a dictatorship. They are the dictators of their own little country. And if you don't adhere to their rules and their regulations they ban you or they kick you out. V/o And a three month ban during peak season could mean the end of your business. Terri Castis is the director commercial development. She denies these allegations. Terri Castis We're trying to balance the interests of 620,000 people, 14 traditional authorities, 14 land claimants, 2 district municipalities, 5 local municipalities, NGO's, subsistence users, recreational users, be they fishermen, be they scuba divers, be they birders – all against the bottom line which is maintaining the ecological integrity of the park. We have a difficult role to play. This is not a personal matter so we need to be really really clear about that. And the rules exist. There's tools, as I said to you in the acts that are enacted, we have legal review teams that look at our actions. What we do has to stand up to public scrutiny. V/o But the business owners say there is no legal process being followed and once you have a fallout with Terri or iSimangaliso, your days are numbered. V/o Last year Grant applied for permission for a group of local surfers to paddle out and put some flowers in the water as part of a global awareness day to save sharks. Grant paddle out It was only gonna take 15 minutes. We were going to say some words and sit around all on the surf boards and just be part of the national drive to drive awareness around sharks. V/o But, while people all over the world were doing this, his request was declined , with iSimangaliso saying they cannot accommodate the event in a Heritage Site as it is not park dependant. V/o Another non-concessionaire who feels he is being victimised is Tokkie Hugo. His original application for a concession was turned down and he says he has been banned twice for debatable reasons. Tokkie So I phoned Terri Castis and I asked her listen Terri what is the story about the banning of me? She said because you're reckless. I said but I wasn't for 3 months even through the gates of your place, of the camp. VO Again Terri denies that they are using their power to victimise people. Terri It's a last resort measure, it's for serious offences – fraud, misrepresentation, endangerment of life – and it's not something we take lightly. And it's not something that we do on the basis of hearsay. V/o But we have a sworn affidavit in our possession in which a holidaymaker alleges that he was personally told [BY WHOM?] that iSimangaliso is out to get Tokkie banned. V/o Shortly after Grant gave up his concession, he was asked to skipper for 3 days for another operator. On day 3, just as he was launching with a boat full of overseas tourists, an Isimangaliso representative handed him a cellphone. Grant Smith I said what are you talking about? How did I fraudulently enter the park? Check your records we've paid and this is the third and last day of launching. What's going on here? Basically he said it's not open for discussion. You will leave or there will be consequences. Terri He hadn't paid his R1,000 for that day and he was merely transporting people onto the beach and he was not doing what he was supposed to be doing to gain that particular access. V/o But Grant showed us proof that the R3000 for the 3 days' launching was indeed paid. In spite of the numerous letters and emails that Grant sent to iSimangaliso, he was banned for three months. V/o The complaints are not just about personal victimisation, but also that Isimangaliso has made Sodwana very tourist-unfriendly, and that this has lead to a decline in tourist numbers. V/o We heard horror stories about disabled people not being able to use the only ablution facilities for disabled people because they didn't have a permit which would give their vehicle access to the beach. Terri People who have people in the family who are disabled, or are disabled themselves must avail themselves of the ability to apply for a permit at Oceans and Coast and that will resolve the issue. V/o Not necessarily. Sandra Wright applied for two permits for her best friends’ two wheelchair bound sons, more than six months prior to their December holiday. By the time they arrived in Sodwana, they had not yet received the original signed permits. Sandra And when I got all the permits emailed and they printed it for me. I then went to the gate and showed the gentleman. He said to me unfortunately he's not in a position to give the go-ahead. V/o In the end, despite numerous phone calls, they were denied vehicle access, because they could not produce original permits, and the two sons had to sit at home for the entire holiday. LINK This is the only road that all tourists, tractors and operators use to move their boats but since Isimangaliso Management has taken over road maintenance has been a problem. Manie One of the local members driven to Richard's Bay with a truck and he's gone and he fetched 2 loads of tar. They've hired compactors, and they've hired all the correct machines. The guys came back to Sodwana and they started fixing the biggest holes. We didn't ask Isimangaliso for any contribution. Only to find approximately a week later Isimangaliso have sent a team of workers to open up the holes that we've just closed up with the tar. They dug the tar out and they put gravel and sand in the holes. Terri On that particular issue the people had absolutely no environmental authorisation to do what they were doing. We have an obligation, a statutory obligation to stop work in that instance. And to review the situation and we then went in and did a repair, which as I said to you in a matter of months will have broken up because of the structural damage on the road. VO But Andre Nel, a Sodwana regular who happens to be a civil engineer, disagrees. Andre Rather keep the premix, cold-mix, whatever they've used. As long as it's got a cohesive material in keep it there because at least the hole will remain closed. V/o Isimangaliso claims that there has been a 900% increase in the number of tourism establishments in Sodwana. On the ground, there are signs of a different picture. V/o Since they took over, at least 5 diving companies in Sodwana closed down, and 6 major fishing competitions that used to be hosted here have now moved elsewhere. Even the amount of concession holders dwindled by almost two thirds according to figures given to us by the locals. Jabulani A lot of business people they are no longer surviving just because they've got many rules that affect them. Right now people they lost their job. V/o For every company that closes down, it means four or five local families who lose their income. And higher unemployment often leads to a higher crime rate. Manie In the last 12 months, armed robberies that I know about personally. I know about 12 armed robberies in Sodwana, in our community here. Andre Nel is on crutches at the moment after he was shot by a robber inside iSimangaliso's campsite. Andre As we got to the outside a shot went off. He shot me through the femur, my upper leg, I fell right there and then and he just walked off into the distance. V/o Two months ago one of Tokkie's regular guests Thys Beselaar was visiting him with his father when three armed robbers suddenly walked through the door. Tokkie And the next moment the guy with the shotgun he shoot him. He was lying there and then I go in and I had a hell of a fight with the two guys – the one with the 9mm and the guy with the AK47. Luckily, luckily I won them and they run away. V/o Thys died a few days later from the shotgun wound V/o A whole group of Sodwana businessmen are now taking iSimangaliso to court. Lawyer I represent approximately 50 clients that reside and do business in the Sodwana area and everyone that I've spoken to complained bitterly about the capricious and arbitrary way in which the director of commercial development, Terri Castis, and the CEO of iSimangaliso Wetland Park Authority, Andre Zaloumis have been conducting the activities of the wetland park authority. Terri Well, lawyers have views and the lawyer you've consulted has a view and our legal team has a different view. LINK There's an old African saying that goes “when 2 elephants fight it is the grass that gets trampled”. In this situation the grass represents the poorest of the poor in the Sodwana community. V/o And because the community can't afford to fight Isimangaliso in court, they started using protest action against iSimangaliso. First they stopped them from building the new gate because they say they were not consulted and the land is still subject to a land claim. Then they blocked the road between Hluhluwe and Sodwana, where it runs through the iSimangaliso Park. UPSOUND Isimangaliso promised people to give a job but no job. Terri There's been a dispute with 2 land claimants for quite some time. We have held off in the hopes that the 2 groups would resolve their differences but they haven't. And we now have to proceed. We have no option in the interest of the environment in the interest of Job creation and in the interest of tourism. Jabulani What we are doing now, we are just waiting then once they want to start something it's where we can stop them. And if they don't want to do that thing we just fight together and stop everything going to Sodwana Bay there. V/o So will Sodwana survive? And will our first proclaimed world heritage site survive? Only time will tell. Jabulani So that is the problem of iSimangaliso. They think they are the god of this area. Terri In the next few years we've secured R368milion to invest in the park. A substantial amount of which will go into Sodwana Bay because it is the goose that lays the golden eggs. Andre My experience there is imprinted in my head - northern KZN and specifically that area there I will definitely not visit again. Studio outtro Isimangaliso reports to the national minister of the environment. We tried in vain to get an interview from her on this topic... Promo1 V/o Sodwana Bay is no longer the ocean lover's paradise that it used to be Soundup Manie I will take you from one place to the next. People who want to sell their properties V/o What went wrong in South Africa's first proclaimed World Heritage Site? Promo2 V/o The town of Sodwana in Northern KZN seems to be struggling. And, they're blaming the managing authority of the World heritage Site for their woes Soundup Jabulani That is the problem with Isimangaliso. They think they are the God of this area Promo3 Soundup Terri There has been a 900% increase in the number of establishments in the Sodwana Bay area V/o But that is not the whole story. Something seems to have gone terribly wrong in this little piece of paradise

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Is tourism delivering on its promises of job creation. Claire travels to Sodwana to find out...
metadata.Summary: Isimangaliso is an organ of state appointed to run and develop the area formerly known as the Greater St Lucia Wetland Park. It is a world heritage site, so declared during the fight to stop government from mining the dunes around St Lucia. At the time, figures were quoted showing that the tourism industry could earn much more money than mining would bring in, and that it would create more jobs and upliftment for the people living around the park. In the almost 20 years since Isimangaliso took over they have achieved a lot. But, especially around the Sodwana area, there seems to be growing unhappiness about the way things are done (or is not being done) Although many of the problems with service delivery actually fall under other government departments, the people are blaming Isimangaliso. And now they want their land back from the park. Fences are being cut weekly and protests are staged at the gates of Isimangaliso.Will all this threaten the existence of South Africa's first world heritage site?
metadata.Further information: We will look at the problems of the local communities and the tourism based businesses on the border of the park in the Sodwana region. We will interview people from the different groups and of course also interview Isimangaliso. We've already filmed some of the protests, and have a host of archive material on the area
